A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LittleBit-2 research and contain 21 readable pages, including Appendices A–J. Text and rendered-page comparisons establish complete correspondence of the scientific material; differences concern the title, publication metadata and limited layout changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic reconstruction experiments, LLM benchmark results and ablations in Section 5 and Tables 1–3, with additional empirical analyses and generated samples in Appendices D–G and I.

after.justification: v2 retains the same original experiments, benchmark outcomes, ablations, appendix analyses and generated samples. Their retention from v1 does not alter their status as original empirical results.

M1.justification: The low-rank binary architecture, Joint-ITQ objective and alternating updates, scale extraction, and training/inference procedures are unchanged. Algorithms 1–2 and the reference implementations in Appendix J are identical.

E1.justification: Both retain synthetic spectral reconstruction, WikiText-2 perplexity, and HellaSwag, ARC-Easy, ARC-Challenge, PIQA and Winogrande evaluation. The weight-analysis coverage in Appendix E and generation scenario in Appendix I are also unchanged.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in every corresponding experiment. Tables 1–4 retain GPTQ, EfficientQAT, BiLLM, ARB-LLM, OneBit, STBLLM, LittleBit, Tiny-Rank FP and Random Rotation in their respective comparisons; appendix comparator sets also match.

E3.justification: Both report the same model configurations, bit budgets, 2048-token perplexity evaluation, zero-shot metrics, baseline group size of 128 and 50 Joint-ITQ iterations. Synthetic experiments, iteration sweeps and residual-comparison protocols are unchanged.

E4.justification: Table 3's component ablations, Figures 7–8's training and sign-flipping analyses, and Appendices E–G's spectral, iteration-sensitivity and residual analyses are identical. Appendix I retains the same qualitative generation examples.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting is unchanged, including the spectral distribution summaries in Figures 6 and 11–12. No repeated-run or seed information, uncertainty-estimation procedures, confidence intervals or significance tests are added or revised.

E6.justification: All entries in Tables 1–4, plotted results and Appendix I outputs are unchanged. For example, Table 1 reports LittleBit-2's 1.0-bpp Llama-3 8B result as 11.53 perplexity and 57.33% average accuracy in both versions.

T1.justification: Proposition 4.1, Lemma 4.2, Definition 4.3, Theorem 4.4 and the Appendix A proofs are identical. The residual-architecture reasoning in Appendix G and memory derivations in Appendix H are also unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same spectral-gain diagnosis, Joint-ITQ contribution, sub-1-bit performance claims and absence of additional inference overhead. Adding LittleBit-2 to the title does not change these claims' meaning or scope.

C2.justification: Interpretations of heavy-tailed spectral advantages, geometric alignment, training stability and inherited inference efficiency are unchanged. The applicability qualifications, impact discussion and future directions are also retained without revision.

D1.justification: Initialization details in Appendix C, iteration and timing information in Appendix F, memory accounting in Appendix H and reference code in Appendix J are unchanged. No implementation disclosures or code/data access information are added or revised.

R1.justification: Section 2 and the complete reference list are unchanged. Both versions position the contribution identically relative to LittleBit, other extreme-quantization methods and rotation-based incoherence processing.

P1.justification: v2 adds 'LittleBit-2:' to the title and running headers and replaces the preprint notice with an ICML 2026/PMLR 306 proceedings and copyright notice. The arXiv version/date stamp also changes; body prose, section order and appendix structure remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The expanded publication notice and associated spacing cause text reflow across pages 1–2, including a contribution bullet continuing onto page 2. Figures 1–14, Tables 1–4, algorithms and code listings retain their content and design; pages 3–21 differ visually only in their running headers.

improvement.justification: v2 identifies LittleBit-2 in the title and updates publication metadata, with minor reflow on pages 1–2. The scientific argument, empirical evidence, claims and reproducibility material remain unchanged, including all appendices. These limited presentation edits have no meaningful net effect on overall paper quality.
